newsitem.title: CANADA: AlphaStar ready to start DTH service.
newsitem.headline: AlphaStar ready to start DTH service.

text.p: AlphaStar Canada Inc, a subsidiary of Tee-Comm Electronics Inc, has cleared its last hurdle before it starts its direct-to-home television service in Canada, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
"We have everything we need now," Clive Hobson, a spokesman for AlphaStar Canada, said in a phone interview from Milton, Ontario. The first subscriber will receive the service next Tuesday, he said.
Canada's industry minister announced on Thursday that AlphaStar has been granted permission to use a U.S. satellite link to provide its DTH service.

Federal government policy requires Canadian satellite broadcasting distribution services to make use of Canadian facilities, but a 1972 agreement allows the use of foreign satellites if Canada has a shortage.
Canada has been short on satellite space since one of its major satellites broke down about a year ago.
But none of the other Canadian companies preparing to set up direct-to-home broadcasting services have applied to use U.S. satellite space, a spokesman for Industry Canada said in an interview.

Companies would need approval from both Industry Canada and the Canadian Radio-Television and Telecommunications Commission in order to be granted permission to use U.S. satellite links, Industry Canada spokesman Carl Olsen said.
The companies would have to assure the officials that they will use Canadian space as soon as it is available and show that they have a substantial subscriber base, he said.
But other companies may have a hard time finding available satellite capacity in the United States too, said Hobson.
"If you went shopping for satellites, you'd be hard pressed," he said.
AlphaStar acquired extra U.S. space previously through its U.S. counterparts on expectations of a Canadian shortage of capacity, Hobson explained.
"We had the satellite space in hand," Hobson said.
The company was granted a DTH licence last week. It aims to supply 75 channels by the end of March and 110 channels in June, Hobson said.
